beats.script_body: Built in the 1960s, this imposing arts campus replaced a neighborhood of tenements called San Juan Hill — gleefully bulldozed by urban planner Robert Moses — a predominantly African American neighborhood where the exterior shots for the movie West Side Story were filmed. Beyond being a controversial urban-planning move, Lincoln Center wasn't well received architecturally: it was relentlessly criticized for its conservative design, fortresslike aspect and poor acoustics. For the center's 50th anniversary, in 2009 to 2010, Diller Scofidio + Renfro and other architects gave the complex a critically acclaimed freshening up.

beats.script_body: This compelling little museum, housed in a three-story town house from 1898, is one of Manhattan's best-kept secrets. beats.script_body: The stretch of Manhattan west of Central Park was once a lively mix of African American, Latino and German Jewish immigrant communities — which is where you'll find some of the best smoked fish in town. In more recent decades it has become a base for well-to-do artsy types, young professionals and the stroller set. Beyond the chain stores along Broadway, the neighborhood is an architectural bonanza of beaux arts, baroque, neo-Gothic and postwar styles.
